title: Classes & Objects
description: Learn how to model game entities with classes, objects, fields, properties, constructors, and methods in C#.
completionText: You are ready to use object-oriented design to build larger C# applications and game systems.

lessons.title: Introduction to Classes
objectives: Explain a class as a blueprint for objects.
theory: A class defines the data and behaviour that objects of a particular kind will have. A Player class can describe every player, while each Player object represents one specific player.
The new keyword creates an object from a class. Each object has its own instance data, so two players can have different names and scores.
Good classes model one clear concept. In a game, classes might represent players, enemies, weapons, inventory items, or quests.
terms: A definition used to create objects.
An instance created from a class.
A specific object belonging to a class.
lessons.tryIt: Create a Player class with name and health fields, then create one Player object and print its values.
lessons.challenge: Create two Enemy objects with different names and health values. Display both objects.
mistakes: A class definition does not create an object by itself.
Use new to create an instance.
Access instance fields through an object variable.
Give classes and fields meaningful names.
lessons.summary: Classes define a type of object. The new keyword creates instances, and each instance stores its own values.
quiz: A class defines the structure and behaviour of objects.
An object is a specific instance created from a class.
The dot accesses a member on an object.
Can two objects have different values?
Each instance has its own instance data.

lessons.title: Fields and Properties
theory: A field stores data directly inside a class. A property provides a controlled way to read or change a value using get and set.
Keeping data private protects an object's internal state. A property can allow other code to read a value while only the class can change it.
Use properties when validation or controlled access matters, such as preventing a player's health from becoming negative.
terms: A controlled way to access data.
Accessible only within its containing class.
Protecting internal state behind a public interface.
lessons.tryIt: Create a Character class with a public Name property and a Health property that cannot be changed directly outside the class.
lessons.challenge: Add validation so TakeDamage cannot reduce Health below zero.
mistakes: Do not expose every field publicly without a reason.
private members cannot be accessed from unrelated classes.
A property is not the same as a method.
Validate values before changing state.
lessons.summary: Properties provide controlled access to data. Encapsulation protects object state and keeps values valid.
quiz: private limits access to the containing class.
Properties expose controlled get and set operations.
The class controls assignment while readers can still access it.
Encapsulation protects implementation details and state.

lessons.title: Constructors
objectives: Use this to refer to the current object.
theory: A constructor is a special member that runs when an object is created. It has the same name as the class and no return type.
Constructors establish a valid starting state. A parameterised constructor receives values so each object can be initialised with the data it needs.
A class can have multiple constructors with different parameter lists. This is called constructor overloading.
terms: A member that initialises a new object.
Input supplied to a method or constructor.
A reference to the current object.
Multiple members with different parameter lists.
lessons.tryIt: Create a Weapon class with a constructor that receives a name and damage value.
lessons.challenge: Add a second constructor that creates a default weapon with no arguments.
mistakes: Constructors do not have a return type.
The constructor name must match the class name.
Initialise required properties in the constructor.
Pass arguments in the correct order and type.
lessons.summary: Constructors run during object creation and establish the object's initial valid state.
quiz: Does a constructor have a return type?
What must match the class name?
The constructor has the class name.
Parameters supply values to initialise the object.
Overloads share a name but accept different parameters.

lessons.title: Instance Methods
theory: An instance method is behaviour that belongs to an object. A Player object might have Heal, Jump, or AddScore methods.
Instance methods can read and change the current object's state. A method can return a value when its caller needs a result, or use void when it performs an action without returning data.
Methods should have one clear responsibility and should use parameters for information supplied by the caller.
terms: A return type meaning no value is returned.
The result sent back by a method.
An action an object can perform.
lessons.tryIt: Add Heal and IsAlive methods to your Character class.
lessons.challenge: Build a Player class with methods to add score, lose health, and report whether the player has won.
mistakes: Call instance methods on an object.
Keep method names descriptive.
Return a value when the caller needs an answer.
Keep each method focused.
lessons.summary: Instance methods give objects behaviour and allow them to manage their own state.
quiz: Where does an instance method belong?
Instance methods belong to objects created from a class.
void methods perform an action without returning a value.
How is an instance method called?
The dot accesses the method on an object.
Parameters let callers provide required information.
What should a method usually have?
Focused methods are easier to understand and test.

lessons.title: Static Members
objectives: Call static methods through a class.
theory: A static member belongs to the class itself rather than to one object. It can be used without creating an instance.
Static members suit shared utilities and values common to the whole type. Instance members represent data or behaviour that differs between objects.
Static state is shared by every caller, so use it deliberately.
terms: A member belonging to the class itself.
Data accessed by all users of a type.
lessons.tryIt: Create a static method that converts game minutes into seconds.
lessons.challenge: Create ScoreTools methods for doubling a score and checking a pass mark.
mistakes: Do not call an instance member as if it were static.
Static data is shared, not copied per object.
Use static only when object state is unnecessary.
Call static members through the class name.
lessons.summary: Static members belong to the class and are useful for shared utilities. Instance members belong to individual objects.
quiz: Static members belong to the type itself.
How do you call a static method?
Static methods are called through their class.
When is an instance member useful?
Instance members store or use per-object data.
All callers see the same static state.
What should static state be used for?
Static state is appropriate only when sharing is intentional.

lessons.title: Inheritance
theory: Inheritance lets a derived class reuse members from a base class. A Mage is a Character, so Mage can inherit common name and health behaviour from Character.
The colon in class Mage : Character declares the inheritance relationship. Derived classes can add their own members.
Inheritance models an is-a relationship. If the relationship is has-a, composition is usually clearer: a Player has an Inventory.
terms: The class whose members are inherited.
A class that inherits from another class.
Reusing and extending a base class.
Building a type from other objects.
lessons.tryIt: Create a Character base class and derive Warrior and Mage classes from it.
lessons.challenge: Give Warrior a Strength property and Mage a Mana property while keeping Name in the base class.
mistakes: Inheritance should represent an is-a relationship.
Use base to call the base constructor.
Do not duplicate common members.
Prefer composition for has-a relationships.
lessons.summary: Inheritance allows a derived class to reuse and extend a base class. Use it for clear is-a relationships.
quiz: A derived class receives members from a base class.
What does class Mage : Character mean?
base forwards values to the base class constructor.

lessons.title: Polymorphism and Interfaces
theory: Polymorphism allows code to work with a common type while each derived object provides its own behaviour.
A base method marked virtual can be replaced by a derived class using override.
An interface defines a contract that a class promises to provide. Interfaces are useful when unrelated classes share a capability, such as being damageable.
terms: A method that derived classes may replace.
A derived implementation of a virtual member.
lessons.tryIt: Create an IDamageable interface and implement it in an Enemy class.
lessons.challenge: Create two different IDamageable types and write a method that damages either one through the interface.
mistakes: Implement every required interface member.
Use override only for an inherited virtual member.
Use a shared base type or interface for polymorphism.
Keep interfaces focused on capabilities.
lessons.summary: Polymorphism supports interchangeable implementations, while interfaces define capabilities different classes can share.
quiz: Interfaces describe members a class promises to implement.
Can unrelated classes share an interface?
Interfaces can describe a shared capability.
What must an implementing class provide?
The class must fulfil the interface contract.

lessons.title: Object-Oriented Game Project
objectives: Plan a small object-oriented game system.
Combine classes, constructors, properties, and methods.
theory: Object-oriented design breaks a game into collaborating objects. A Player can hold health and score, an Enemy can hold health and damage, and a Battle can coordinate their interactions.
Identify nouns that may become classes and verbs that may become methods. Keep each class responsible for one concept.
Test each class separately, then test the interactions between objects.
terms: The work a class should own.
The current data held by an object.
lessons.tryIt: Build a Player and Enemy class, then make the player take damage and display updated health.
lessons.challenge: Extend the project with score, an enemy attack method, and a win condition. Test three scenarios.
mistakes: Do not put every responsibility into one class.
Protect state changes with methods when validation is needed.
Test normal and boundary values.
Keep object responsibilities clear.
lessons.summary: Classes and objects model game entities. Constructors, properties, methods, and collaboration create maintainable game systems.
quiz: Focused responsibilities make designs easier to maintain.
Individual behaviour and collaboration need testing.
The project applies the module's object-oriented concepts.
